*
 Judgment
The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/ for the injuries
sustained by him in the road traffic accident caused on 11.09.2014.
02.
The brief facts are as under: It i

s submitted that on 11.09.2014 at about 08.00 a.m when the petitioner was doing work in front of his house at Lingapatna Village, at that time a Motor Cycle bearing No.KA11EC8056 came at high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to this the petitioner sustained (SCCH3) 3 M.V.C.No.1018/2020 grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was admitted to Mathrushree Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, Channapatna and took conservative treatment as inpatient and still he is under treatment as outpatient.

entities.text: Mathrushree Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, Channapatna
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner had spent Rs.25,000/ towards medical expenses.
That the petitioner prior to accident was hale and healthy and was doing agriculture coolie work and earning Rs.20,000/ p.m.
Due to the accident he has become disabled to do his avocation and lost his earning capacity.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle rider.
Even a criminal case is registered against the Motor Cycle rider.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said Motor Cycle and hence both are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence this petition.
03. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before this court and hence he was placed absent through out the proceedings of the petition.
However the respondent No.2 have appeared before this Court through their counsel and filed written statement.
The averments of the written statement of the respondent No.2 is as under: It is false that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent riding of rider of motorcycle.
It is false that due to the accident he had sustained disability and lost earning capacity.
The Motor Cycle rider does not possess valid driving licence on the date of accident.
There is a delay of 36 days in filing FIR and the offending Motor Cycle has falsely implicated in this case.
That the petitioner was working in the middle of road without taking any precaution.
Hence he had sustained injuries due to his negligence.
The claim of the petitioner is excessive and hence this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
05. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 07 documents as Ex.P.1 to 7 and closed his side.
06. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 submit no oral evidence.
But the copy of policy was marked as Ex.R.1 with consent.
07. Heard both sides.
The petitioner and respondent No.2 have filed written arguments.

sentences.text: Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor:

ISSUES 01.Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 11.09.2014 at about 08.00 a.m. on Lingapatna Village, Halaguru Hobli, Malavalli Taluk, Mandya District, due to rash and negligent act of the riding of the Motor Cycle bearing reg. No.KA11EC 8056 by it rider as alleged in the petition?
02.Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?
09. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under: Issue No.1 In negative Issue No.2 In negative Issue No.3

As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is the grievance of the petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries due (SCCH3) 6 M.V.C.No.1018/2020 to the rash and negligent driving of Motor Cycle rider driver.
Due to the accident he had sustained disability and put into hardship.
The same was opposed by the respondent No.2 and contended that the accident did not took place due to the negligence of Motor Cycle rider but he had sustained injuries due to his negligence only.
Hence they are not liable to pay compensation.
11. In order to prove this, the petitioner himself got examined as PW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the petition in his affidavit.
The PW.1 in his cross examination has admitted that "That one Prakash was riding the motorcycle.
That the accident took place on 11.09.2014.
That I had filed this petition after 06 years of accident because earlier counsel to whom I had furnished documents did not proceed with the case.
It is true that there is delay of 36 days in lodging complaint to the police.
It is true that in Ex.P.6 the vehicle number is not mentioned.
I have not produced MLC extract and police intimation.
I have not produced the spot sketch.
It is true that the offending vehicle dashed to me and it fell on road.
That I was standing in front of my house at about 08.00 a.m.
It is true that in Ex.P.6 the time of accident is mentioned as 07.00 a.m. (SCCH3) 7 M.V.C.No.1018/2020 It is true that I was standing on road.
It is true that in the said road two vehicles can passed.
After the accident I lost consciousness.
That the neighbours of my house have intimated me about the offending vehicle number.
It is true that I have not stated the vehicle number at the hospital because as the matter was intended to be compromised".

The PW.1 has denied other suggestion of the respondent No.2.
12.
The PW.1 in support of the case had got marked entire police records as per Ex.P.1 to 7.

On perusal of these documents, it is clear that the concerned I.O after investigation has filed Charge sheet against Motor Cycle rider for the alleged offences punishable U/s 279, 337 of IPC and U/Sec Sri.Ningegowda vs Sri.Nagesha on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34957406/
3 187 of IMV Act for the reason that the petitioner sustained injuries due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle rider only.

13. Eventhough the respondent No.2 has contend that the accident did not occurred due to the negligence of Motor Cycle rider and it is due to the negligence of petitioner himself, but they have not produced any supportive oral and documentary evidence to prove their defence.

It is true that the copy of policy was got marked as Ex.R.1 with consent which (SCCH3) 8 M.V.C.No.1018/2020 shows that on the date of accident the policy issued in the name of the respondent No.1 was valid.
14. The petitioner has produced mahazar along with sketch as per Ex.P.3.
It is true that as per Ex.P.3 the accident took place in front of petitioner's house that too by the side of edge of road.
So this shows that the petitioner was working in front of his house i.e on the road which is not permissible one.
The petitioner might had working without noticing the vehicles on going on the road.
This shows that there is negligence of the petitioner also.
15. It is pertinent to note that the petitioner eventhough produced police records, but not able to prove the occurrence of alleged accident.
As per Ex.P.5 the IMV report it is stated no damages to the offending vehicle.
If at all the accident really took place then atleast the scratch or a mark would be found on the offending vehicle.
Hence the alleged negligence of the rider of motorcycle cannot be ascertained.
16. Further the petitioner has not got marked any of the medical records to show that he had sustained injuries and he had obtained treatment.

Even there is no MLC extract, police intimation,
outpatient records, medical bills, prescriptions.
The (SCCH3) 9 M.V.C.No.1018/2020 police records are not supported with the medical records to believe that really on 11.09.2014 the accident occurred and the petitioner has sustained injuries.
17. The petitioner has stated that he could not produce medical bills as he had furnished the same to his earlier counsel and they have not returned it.
Even for a while if we assume it as true then what prevented the petitioner atleast to obtain copies of it and then to produced the same before this court.
Even the PW.1 had admitted in his cross examination that he had not mentioned the vehicle number at hospital as the matter would be compromised.
So there is no entry of RTA in any of the hospital.

Atleast the petitioner has not produced any supportive documents to show that he had obtained treatment with respect to the injuries sustained in road traffic accident occurred on 11.09.2014.
18.
It is true that there is delay in filing complaint and petition by the petitioner.
Eventhough it is not fatal to the case of the petitioner but the petitioner has not established the occurrence of the accident itself.
Moreover the petitioner at the time of accident did not noticed the rider of motorcycle and its (SCCH3) 10 M.V.C.No.1018/2020 number.
Then he came to know about the vehicle number through his neighbours.
But then also the same is not mentioned in the complaint.
Even there are no supportive documents to show that another petition was not filed before Mandya court and the petitioner had not obtained any compensation.
Sri. Ningegowda

vs Sri.Nagesha on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34957406/
4 19.
Hence only based upon some police records it cannot be presumed that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle.
Therefore the petitioner failed to prove his case.
Hence with the available documents on records, I am of opinion that the petitioner has not proved that he had sustained injuries only due to the rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle rider.
Hence, I answered issue No.1 in negative.
20. Issue No.2:
In view of my above finding when the petitioner has not proved the occurrence of the accident itself, then he is not entitled for any compensation.
21. Regarding liability: As stated above the petitioner has not proved the he had sustained injuries due to rash and negligent riding of rider of motorcycle.
It is true that the said motorcycle is owned by the respondent No.1 and duly insured with the respondent (SCCH3) 11 M.V.C.No.1018/2020 No.2.
But the respondents are not liable to indemnify the petitioner as he had not proved occurrence of the accident itself.
Hence I answered the issue No.2 in negative.
22. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec. 166 of the M.V. Act is hereby dismissed, with costs.
The advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, got typed by him, then corrected and pronounced by me in open court, on this the 20th day of January 2023).
(SHILPA.K.S) VII Addl. Judge and ACMM, Bengaluru.
